claim_verdicts.evidence: "A service account is a type of non-human account that, in Kubernetes, provides a distinct identity in a Kubernetes cluster." / "Namespaced: Each service account is bound to a Kubernetes namespace." Table: Intended use — ServiceAccount: Workloads, automation; User: People. (refs mirror is kubernetes/website at v1.37; text unchanged in meaning for 1.34.)

"Kubernetes automatically creates a ServiceAccount object named `default` for every namespace"; ServiceAccount admission controller: "If the pod does not have a `.spec.serviceAccountName` set, the admission controller sets the name of the ServiceAccount for this incoming Pod to `default`." Capture on kind v1.34.11 lists `default` in a fresh security-lessons.

"Provided that neither the ServiceAccount's automountServiceAccountToken field nor the Pod's ... is set to false: ... adds a volumeMount to each container ... mounted at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount". Projected volume sources: token, ca.crt, namespace. Capture lists ca.crt, namespace, token in with-token.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/.../access-authn-authz/service-accounts-admin.md (ServiceAccount admission controller; Bound service account token volume); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-accounts.txt

claim_verdicts.evidence: "A serviceAccountToken source, that contains a token that the kubelet acquires from kube-apiserver. The kubelet fetches time-bound tokens using the TokenRequest API. ... The kubelet also refreshes that token before the token expires."

"A service account is an automatically enabled authenticator that uses signed bearer tokens to verify requests." "The created token is a signed JSON Web Token (JWT)." "The private key is used to sign generated service account tokens." The lesson itself only says "a signed credential that names one ServiceAccount", which this supports.

"Service accounts authenticate with the username system:serviceaccount:(NAMESPACE):(SERVICEACCOUNT), and are assigned to the groups system:serviceaccounts and system:serviceaccounts:(NAMESPACE)." authentication.md l.52: an authenticated caller is a member of "the special group system:authenticated". Capture (kind v1.34.11): Groups [system:serviceaccounts system:serviceaccounts:security-lessons system:authenticated].

Round 2: lesson now reads "may do only what bindings naming it or its groups allow, and anything else gets 403 Forbidden". authorization.md: "All parts of an API request must be allowed by some authorization mechanism ... access is denied by default." controlling-access.md l.125: "the modules deny the request, then the request is denied (HTTP status code 403)."

"Default RBAC policies grant scoped permissions to control-plane components, nodes, and controllers, but grant no permissions to service accounts outside the kube-system namespace (beyond the permissions given by API discovery roles)." system:basic-user, bound to system:authenticated: "read-only access to basic information about themselves". Capture: list pods / get secrets / create deployments all no.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/.../access-authn-authz/rbac.md (ServiceAccount permissions; Default roles and role bindings); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-accounts.txt
